methods.name: Bank of China: convert and wire to your own US account
methods.verdict: Best fully priced route for large sums
methods.who: Foreign passport holder whose CNY is lawful China current-account income (for example salary) and who can show the amount and the tax paid.
methods.limit: No fixed cap in the rule; the bank converts what your documents support.
methods.cost: FX margin 0.2100% + commission 1‰ (CNY 50–260) + cable CNY 150 + USD 25 full-amount delivery + receiving-bank fee.
pros: Bank fees are capped, so the percentage cost falls as the amount grows
Every price is published by the bank
Legal basis is explicit for foreign individuals
cons: Needs tax vouchers matching the amount
Branch visit and bank review
Above USD 50,000 per payment a tax-filing form may be asked for

steps.t: Collect proof that the CNY is lawful China income, showing amounts: employment contract or payslips and your individual income tax payment record.
Take your passport and the documents to the bank that holds the account.
For a single payment above USD 50,000, ask the bank whether it needs a tax-filing form; if so, file it with the local tax office first.
Ask the bank to convert the CNY to USD at its telegraphic selling rate. The board rate is a reference; the rate at the moment of the transaction applies.
Order a SWIFT wire to your US account and choose full-amount delivery so correspondent charges are a fixed USD 25 instead of a deduction.
Pay the commission (1‰, minimum CNY 50, maximum CNY 260) and the CNY 150 cable fee.
Send the whole documented amount in one wire. Do not split it into smaller pieces to avoid review.
When the wire arrives your US bank may charge an incoming-wire fee (Chase: USD 15).
Keep the conversion slip and wire receipt, and file the FBAR and Form 8938 if the account passed the thresholds during the year.

methods.name: HSBC China (Premier or Advance): convert and wire
methods.verdict: Fees published, exchange rate not — compare on the day
methods.who: Same legal basis as M01, for customers of HSBC China. Premier needs an average balance of CNY 500,000.
methods.limit: No fixed cap in the rule; the bank converts what your documents support.
methods.cost: Commission 0.1% (CNY 100–500) + cable CNY 120 + CNY 200 pre-collected for full-amount delivery. FX margin not published.
pros: Same bank group on both sides if you also bank with HSBC abroad
Fees are capped
HSBC Global Transfer to your own HSBC account abroad is free on Premier (CNY 145 on Advance), so only the conversion is left to price
cons: Exchange rate not verified, so no all-in total
Higher fee cap than Bank of China
Correspondent charges above CNY 200 are collected later
The free Global Transfer only works between HSBC accounts, and its rate is still unpublished

steps.t: Prepare the same evidence as for M01: passport, proof of the income amount and tax vouchers.
Ask for the bank's selling rate before you confirm and compare it with the Bank of China board.
Order the outward telegraphic transfer; pay 0.1% (minimum CNY 100, maximum CNY 500) plus CNY 120 cable.

If you also hold an HSBC account abroad, ask for HSBC Global Transfer to your own same-name account: free on Premier, CNY 145 on Advance, per the same tariff. The conversion from CNY to USD is still charged at the bank's own rate.
If you want the full USD amount delivered, the bank pre-collects CNY 200 toward overseas agent charges and bills any shortfall later.
Complete the US filings as in M01.

methods.name: Another mainland bank (ICBC, CCB, ABC, CMB and others)
methods.verdict: Same rule, prices not verified
methods.who: Same legal basis as M01 at whichever bank holds your account.
methods.limit: No fixed cap in the rule; the bank converts what your documents support.
pros: No need to move the money to another bank first
cons: No official tariff was verified for these banks
Staff experience with foreign customers varies

steps.t: Prepare passport, proof of the income amount and tax vouchers.
Ask the bank for its published tariff and selling rate, then proceed as in M01.

methods.name: Foreign Permanent Resident ID: annual facilitation quota
methods.verdict: Annual quota applies if you hold the card
methods.who: Foreign individuals who hold a China Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card.
methods.limit: USD 50,000 equivalent per person per year.
pros: The annual facilitation quota applies to you
cons: Few foreigners hold the card
Above the quota you are back to M01 with documents
Splitting or using other people's quotas is prohibited

steps.t: Show the Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card at the bank and buy up to the annual quota.
Wire the USD as in M01.
For anything above the quota use M01 with tax vouchers; do not split or borrow quotas.

methods.name: Convert back CNY you originally exchanged from foreign currency
methods.verdict: Simplest route if the CNY came from dollars you brought in less than 24 months ago
methods.who: Foreign individual holding unused CNY that was obtained by exchanging foreign currency in China.
methods.limit: The unused part of the amount on the original exchange memo, within 24 months of the exchange date.
pros: Needs only your ID and the original exchange memo
No tax voucher is mentioned for this case
cons: Only within 24 months of the original exchange
Only up to what the memo shows
Useless without the original memo

steps.t: Find the original exchange memo (兑换水单) from when you turned foreign currency into CNY; it is valid for converting back for 24 months from the exchange date.
Take your passport and the memo to the bank and convert the unused CNY back to foreign currency.
Wire the USD to your own account as in M01.

methods.name: House-sale proceeds
methods.verdict: Use when the CNY came from selling property
methods.who: Foreign individual who sold a home on the mainland.
methods.limit: The sale proceeds supported by the contract and tax voucher.
methods.cost: Bank charges as M01, plus China tax on the gain (20% of gain).
pros: Explicitly remittable
Large single amounts are normal for this route
cons: Tax voucher required; tax-filing form above USD 50,000
Approval path differs by city

steps.t: Pay the tax on the sale and obtain the tax voucher. Gain is taxed at 20% of proceeds less original value and reasonable expenses.
Bring passport, the house transfer contract and registration certificate, and the tax voucher.
If the amount exceeds USD 50,000, file the tax-filing form for external payments.
The bank (with SAFE approval where required) converts and remits the proceeds.
In the US, report the sale on your return and claim a credit for the China tax.

methods.name: Emigrant property transfer (移民财产转移)
methods.verdict: For former mainland residents moving their pre-emigration assets
methods.who: A person who emigrated from China and transfers property lawfully owned before emigrating.
methods.limit: The amount approved by SAFE; may be sent in one or several wires.
methods.cost: Bank charges as M01 once approved.
pros: Covers savings and assets that are not recent salary
Since 2014: no staged instalments, no head-office filing, no notarisation
cons: SAFE branch approval and tax certificate required
Wire only to your own overseas account
Property without provable lawful source is refused

steps.t: Apply to the SAFE branch of your former household registration.
Submit proof of lawful source and tax certificates or tax-payment vouchers.
After approval the bank may remit the approved amount in one or several wires.
Funds go directly to your own account abroad; foreign cash may not be withdrawn in China.

methods.name: Inheritance transfer (继承财产转移)
methods.verdict: For money inherited from someone in China
methods.who: A foreign citizen who lawfully inherits an estate in China.
methods.limit: The amount approved by SAFE; may be sent in one or several wires.
methods.cost: Bank charges as M01 once approved.
pros: Dedicated legal route for inherited money
Several inheritances can be filed together
cons: SAFE branch approval required
US Form 3520 if the bequest exceeds USD 100,000

steps.t: Apply to the SAFE branch where the deceased had household registration.
Submit the inheritance documents and tax certificates or tax-payment vouchers.
After approval the bank remits in one or several wires to your own account abroad.
In the US, file Form 3520 if bequests from a foreign estate exceed USD 100,000 in the year.

methods.name: Dividends and other investment income
methods.verdict: Use when the CNY is investment income
methods.who: Foreign individual with dividends, profit or similar lawful income from China.
methods.limit: The income supported by documents and tax vouchers.
methods.cost: Bank charges as M01; China tax on the income is 20%.
pros: Explicitly listed as a remittable item
cons: Tax filing for single payments above USD 50,000
Treaty and withholding details not reviewed here

steps.t: Make sure the 20% tax on the dividend or interest was withheld and get the voucher.
For a single payment above USD 50,000 complete the tax filing.
Convert and wire at the bank as in M01.

methods.name: Send the money abroad in RMB and convert outside China
methods.verdict: Possible, but the conversion cost is unknown
methods.who: Individuals with lawful current-account RMB income; banks apply know-your-customer and due-diligence review.
methods.cost: Bank of China charges the same commission and cable for an RMB wire. Conversion cost abroad not verified.
pros: No conversion inside China
You choose where and when to convert
cons: Receiving bank must accept CNY
Offshore conversion rate not verified
Still needs proof of lawful income

steps.t: Confirm with the receiving bank that it accepts a CNY wire.
Ask your mainland bank for a cross-border RMB remittance of your current-account income and pass its review.
Pay the cross-border wire commission and cable fee.
Convert to USD at the receiving bank.

methods.name: Wise (from a China bank app or Alipay)
methods.verdict: Convenient for after-tax salary, up to CNY 300,000 per transfer
methods.who: Non-mainland-Chinese nationals who work or worked in China and have a China tax record from the last 3 years.
methods.limit: CNY 300,000 per transfer by bank app, CNY 50,000 by Alipay; overall limit is your after-tax China salary.
methods.cost: Fee shown at quote time; five sampled quotes are in the cost ladder.
pros: No branch visit
Mid-market rate with a visible fee
cons: Per-transfer and salary-based limits
Only to an account you own

steps.t: Check eligibility: not a mainland Chinese national, worked in China, tax record within 3 years.
Upload the tax record; your limit is your after-tax China salary.
Create a CNY to USD transfer to an account in your own name and get the live quote.
Pay from your China bank app (up to CNY 300,000 per transfer) or Alipay (up to CNY 50,000).

methods.name: Western Union through a partner bank
methods.verdict: Not usable for a bank-to-bank transfer right now
methods.who: Customers of partner banks; a passport is accepted as ID, subject to bank restrictions.
pros: Receiver can collect cash without a bank account
cons: Bank-account delivery shown as temporarily unavailable
Fees and limits not published
Banks restrict some countries and passport holders

steps.t: Ask a partner bank branch whether it serves your passport and destination.
Send for cash pick-up and give the receiver the tracking number.

methods.name: Carry USD cash out of China
methods.verdict: Only for small amounts
methods.limit: Up to USD 5,000 without a permit; USD 5,000–10,000 with a bank permit; above USD 10,000 not allowed in principle.
methods.cost: FX margin 0.2100% on the cash purchase; permit fee waived until 2026-12-31.
pros: No wire fees
cons: USD 10,000 ceiling per trip
Theft and loss risk
US report above USD 10,000; breaches fined up to 20%

steps.t: Buy USD cash at the bank (same documents as M01 for a foreign individual).
For USD 5,000–10,000 ask the bank for the carrying permit (携带外汇出境许可证).
Do not carry more than USD 10,000 equivalent.
On arrival in the US, report on FinCEN Form 105 if the total exceeds USD 10,000.

methods.name: Withdraw abroad with a mainland bank card
methods.verdict: Capped at CNY 100,000 a year
methods.who: Holder of a mainland bank card.
methods.limit: CNY 100,000 per person per calendar year; CNY 10,000 per card per day.
methods.cost: Bank of China: CNY 12 + 1% per withdrawal (maximum CNY 112), plus card-scheme rate and ATM-owner surcharge.
pros: No documents at the time of withdrawal
cons: Annual cap is small compared with a large balance
Over 1% in bank fees before the exchange rate
Exceeding the cap suspends withdrawals for the rest of that year and the next

steps.t: Withdraw at an ATM abroad, at most CNY 10,000 equivalent per card per day.
Stop at CNY 100,000 equivalent for the calendar year across all your cards; do not use other people's cards.
Expect CNY 12 + 1% per withdrawal from Bank of China and possibly a surcharge from the ATM owner.

methods.name: Spend it in place: mainland debit or UnionPay card abroad
methods.verdict: No conversion, but not a way to move the balance
methods.who: Anyone with a mainland-issued debit or credit card. Nothing is converted: you spend the CNY where it is.
methods.limit: Overseas cash withdrawal is capped at CNY 100,000 a year across all your cards and CNY 10,000 a day per card; card spending is described by SAFE as unaffected by that notice, but no spending cap is stated.
pros: Avoids the FX margin of a conversion entirely
No branch visit and no remittance paperwork
Card use abroad is expressly said to be unaffected by the 2017 cash-withdrawal notice
cons: Only works for money you are going to spend, not for money you want to hold in USD
The card scheme's exchange rate and any ATM-owner surcharge are not published here
Overseas cash access is suspended for the year and the next if the annual cap is passed

steps.t: Check whether the card is a CNY card or a foreign-currency card, because the settlement currency decides whether a conversion happens at all.
Use the card for purchases abroad; SAFE states the 2017 notice does not affect normal cash withdrawal and consumption.
Keep overseas cash withdrawals inside CNY 100,000 a year in total and CNY 10,000 a day per card, or access is suspended for this year and the next.

methods.name: Carry CNY cash out and exchange abroad
methods.verdict: Negligible capacity
pros: Simple
cons: Limit figure seen only in an excerpt (CNY 20,000 per trip)
Exchange rate abroad not verified

steps.t: Check the current CNY cash limit before travelling.

methods.name: Splitting the amount or borrowing other people's USD 50,000 quotas
methods.verdict: Do not use
methods.cost: Fine up to 30% of the amount; 30%–100% if serious.
cons: Explicitly banned as evading quota supervision
Fines and possible criminal liability
US gift reporting if money arrives from other people

methods.name: Underground banks and private currency swaps
methods.verdict: Do not use
methods.cost: Fine up to 30% of the amount; 30%–100% if serious.
cons: Private or disguised trading of foreign exchange is illegal
Confiscation, fines and possible criminal liability
No recourse if the counterparty disappears

methods.name: False or borrowed documents to buy foreign exchange
methods.verdict: Do not use
methods.cost: Fine up to 30% of the amount; 30%–100% if serious.
cons: Obtaining foreign exchange with false documents is punished as illegal arbitrage
Untrue documents alone: fine up to CNY 50,000 for an individual

methods.name: Crypto (for example buying USDT with CNY)
methods.verdict: Do not use
cons: Exchange between legal tender and virtual currency is an illegal financial activity in China
Banks and payment firms may not serve it
Related civil acts can be void and losses are your own
